intuitive

in-TOO-ih-tiv — something intuitive just feels right without needing to be explained. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Intuitive is known or perceived by intuition; easily and instinctively understood.

The new remote control was so intuitive that even her grandmother figured it out without reading the manual.

Example

A toddler picks up a tablet for the very first time and, without anyone showing her how, immediately starts swiping and tapping to open a game -- a design so intuitive that she uses it exactly as the designers hoped she would.

Being usable instantly, without any instructions, is what makes the tablet intuitive. Unlike 'simple,' which just means easy, intuitive specifically means it feels natural right away.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

natural: Natural means coming easily, without force or training — a motion or a choice can feel natural. It is broad and says nothing about design. Intuitive is praise for a designed thing: it is built so clearly that the natural response is also the correct one.

user-friendly: User-friendly means designed with helpful guidance — clear labels, menus, and hints that make a product pleasant to operate. Intuitive is the stronger compliment: the design needs no guidance at all, because the right way to use it is obvious at first sight.

self-explanatory: Self-explanatory means a thing explains itself — one look tells you what it is for. Intuitive goes a step further: not just clear to look at, but natural to use, so your hands do the right thing without your mind working it out.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

confusing: difficult to understand

complicated: involving many confusing parts

Where it sits · how automatically it comes to you — easy → intuitive → instinctive

easy vs. intuitive: Easy is weaker and more general than intuitive — something easy just doesn't take much effort, while intuitive means it feels natural and obvious without ever being taught.

instinctive vs. intuitive: Instinctive sits above intuitive in how automatic it is: an intuitive design is grasped by a person on the first try, but instinctive describes built-in behavior a creature performs without any thought — a reflex you are born with, not something you figure out.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: upon, into (Latin)

Root — tuit

Root — tuit: to look, to gaze; to watch over (from Latin tueri, 'to look at, to watch')

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: tending to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: In- ('upon, into') + tuit ('to look, to gaze' — from Latin tueri) + -ive ('tending to'): Latin intueri meant 'to look upon, to consider.' Something intuitive, at its root, is understood just by 'looking upon' it, with no need for a deeper explanation.

Use the root in a new word: tuition

Use the root in a new word: tuition: Her parents saved for years to cover the cost of her college tuition.
